note: Definitions, examples, levels and Arabic translations written for Mastering English Library. Levels are our own CEFR guide.

senses.def: large in amount, size or importance
ex: There is substantial evidence for this claim.
The company made a substantial loss last year.
She received a substantial pay rise.

senses.def: strongly made and solid
ex: The castle walls are thick and substantial.

mistake.wrong: There was a substantial of evidence.
mistake.right: There was a substantial amount of evidence.
mistake.note: substantial is an adjective, so it needs a noun after it.

senses.def: to make something or someone gradually weaker or less effective
ex: Constant criticism can undermine confidence.
The scandal undermined public trust in the government.
These results undermine the original theory.

mistake.wrong: This undermines on our efforts.
mistake.right: This undermines our efforts.
mistake.note: undermine takes a direct object, with no preposition.

senses.def: existing as a natural or basic part of something that cannot be removed
ex: Every investment carries inherent risk.
There are dangers inherent in any extreme sport.
Her inherent sense of fairness made her a good judge.

mistake.wrong: The risk is inherent to every plan.
mistake.right: The risk is inherent in every plan.
mistake.note: The usual preposition is in.

senses.def: to make an action or process possible or easier
ex: Technology can facilitate learning.
The new road will facilitate trade between the towns.
A good chair facilitates discussion in a meeting.

mistake.wrong: The app facilitates students to learn.
mistake.right: The app facilitates learning. / The app helps students (to) learn.
mistake.note: Do not use facilitate + person + to-infinitive. Its object is the process, not the person.

senses.def: a difference between two things that should be the same
ex: There was a discrepancy between the two reports.
Auditors found several discrepancies in the accounts.
How do you explain the discrepancy in the figures?

senses.def: to publicly support or recommend a particular idea, plan or way of doing something
ex: Many experts advocate earlier intervention.
Several studies advocate a four-day working week.
She advocates teaching coding in primary schools.

also.def: a person who publicly supports an idea, plan or group
ex: He is a passionate advocate of free education.

mistake.wrong: Experts advocate for to start school later.
mistake.right: Experts advocate starting school later.
mistake.note: advocate + -ing or + noun. In British English, advocate for is less common; never add to.

senses.def: seeming likely to be true, or able to be believed
ex: This is a plausible explanation.
Her story sounded plausible at first.
It is plausible that the data was entered incorrectly.

senses.def: to make something bad less severe, harmful or painful
ex: Measures were taken to mitigate the impact.
Planting trees can help mitigate flooding.
Nothing can mitigate the seriousness of the crime.

mistake.wrong: We need to mitigate against the risk.
mistake.right: We need to mitigate the risk.
mistake.note: Do not confuse mitigate with militate against.

senses.def: a belief or idea
ex: The notion of free will is still debated.
She rejected the notion that women are less ambitious.
I had no notion of what he meant.

senses.def: including everything that is necessary
ex: The report gives a comprehensive overview.
We offer comprehensive insurance.
a comprehensive list of sources

mistake.wrong: The teacher was very comprehensive with me.
mistake.right: The teacher was very understanding with me.
mistake.note: comprehensive means complete. Understanding (sympathetic) is a different word.

senses.def: after something else happened; later
ex: The data was subsequently analysed.
He was arrested and subsequently released.
Subsequently, the policy was withdrawn.

mistake.wrong: Subsequently to the meeting, we left.
mistake.right: Subsequent to the meeting, we left. / After the meeting, we left.
mistake.note: The prepositional phrase uses the adjective: subsequent to.

senses.def: to control or limit something
ex: Our research was constrained by funding.
Growth is constrained by a lack of skilled workers.

senses.def: to force someone to do something
ex: I felt constrained to tell her the truth.

senses.def: able to become strong, healthy or successful again after something bad happens
ex: Children are often remarkably resilient.
The economy has proved resilient despite the crisis.

senses.def: returning to its original shape after being bent or pressed
ex: Rubber is a resilient material.

senses.def: a time or day by which something must be done
ex: We worked late to meet the deadline.
The deadline for applications is 30 June.
I'm sorry, we missed the deadline.

mistake.wrong: We must catch the deadline.
mistake.right: We must meet the deadline.
mistake.note: Say meet or make a deadline, not catch or reach.

senses.def: movement towards a better or more developed situation
ex: You've made real progress this term.
The patient is making good progress.
We need to check our progress every week.

senses.def: movement forward in a particular direction
ex: Heavy snow made progress up the mountain slow.
The course progresses from easy to difficult tasks.

mistake.wrong: She made a big progress. / He made many progresses.
mistake.right: She made a lot of progress. / She made great progress.
mistake.note: progress is uncountable: no a, no plural. In Arabic تقدُّم can be counted, so this mistake is very common.

senses.def: a detailed study of a subject to discover new information
ex: I'm doing research on renewable energy.
Research shows that sleep improves memory.
She has carried out research into climate change.

mistake.wrong: I made a research about it. / Researches show that...
mistake.right: I did some research on it. / Research shows that... / Studies show that...
mistake.note: research is uncountable, and the verb is do or carry out, never make.

senses.def: [U] knowledge or skill that you get from doing a job or activity
ex: An internship helps you gain experience.
Do you have any experience of working with children?
She has ten years' experience in marketing.

senses.def: [C] something that happens to you that affects how you feel
ex: Living abroad was an amazing experience.
We had some strange experiences on that trip.

mistake.wrong: I have three years experiences in sales.
mistake.right: I have three years' experience in sales.
mistake.note: When it means خبرة, experience is uncountable. Use the plural only for تجارب (events).

senses.def: something that it is your job or duty to deal with
ex: It's my responsibility to lock the office.
Parents have a responsibility to protect their children.

senses.def: blame for something that has happened
ex: The manager took responsibility for the error.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

mistake.wrong: Who is the responsible of this project?
mistake.right: Who is responsible for this project? / Who is in charge of this project?
mistake.note: responsible is an adjective and takes for. Do not use it as a noun (المسؤول).

senses.def: the act of watching, listening to or thinking about something carefully
ex: Pay attention to the instructions.
Can I have your attention, please?
The film attracted a lot of attention.

mistake.wrong: Take attention! / Give attention on the road.
mistake.right: Pay attention! / Pay attention to the road.
mistake.note: The verb is pay, and the preposition is to. خُذ بالك is not take attention.

senses.def: [C] a decision or arrangement, often formal and written, between two or more groups
ex: The two sides finally reached an agreement.
They signed a trade agreement.

senses.def: [U] the situation in which people have the same opinion
ex: We're all in agreement on this point.

mistake.wrong: I am agree with you.
mistake.right: I agree with you.
mistake.note: agree is a verb. Do not add am / is / are before it.

senses.def: to stop trying to do something before you have finished
ex: Don't give up! You're nearly there.
I gave up trying to explain.

senses.def: to stop doing something you do regularly
ex: He gave up smoking last year.
I'm giving up sugar for a month.

mistake.wrong: He gave up to smoke.
mistake.right: He gave up smoking.
mistake.note: give up is followed by -ing, not to-infinitive.

senses.def: to take care of someone or something
ex: She looks after her younger brother.
Can you look after my cat while I'm away?

mistake.wrong: I look after my keys but I can't find them.
mistake.right: I'm looking for my keys but I can't find them.
mistake.note: look after = يعتني. look for = يبحث عن.

senses.def: to finish, use or sell all of something so that there is none left
ex: We've run out of milk.
The car ran out of petrol on the motorway.
I'm running out of patience.

mistake.wrong: The milk has run out of.
mistake.right: We've run out of milk. / The milk has run out.
mistake.note: The person is the subject of run out of. The thing can be the subject of run out (without of).

senses.def: to get information about something because you want to know more about it
ex: Can you find out when the train leaves?
I found out that she had lied.

mistake.wrong: I want to know-out the price.
mistake.right: I want to find out the price.
mistake.note: Use find out for getting new information.

senses.def: to start a journey
ex: We set off early to avoid the traffic.

senses.def: to cause an alarm to start ringing, or a bomb to explode
ex: Burnt toast set off the fire alarm.

senses.def: to go somewhere in order to collect someone or something
ex: I'll pick you up at the station.
Can you pick up the dry cleaning?

senses.def: to lift something or someone using your hands
ex: Please pick up your clothes.

senses.def: to learn a skill or language without studying it formally
ex: She picked up Spanish while living in Madrid.

mistake.wrong: I'll pick up you at six.
mistake.right: I'll pick you up at six.
mistake.note: With a pronoun (you, him, it), it must go between pick and up.

senses.def: to write all the necessary information on an official document
ex: Please fill in this form.
Fill in your name and address.

senses.def: an obvious problem or difficult situation that people do not want to talk about
ex: The budget cut was the elephant in the room.
Someone had to mention the elephant in the room.

senses.def: something that has both good and bad effects
ex: Fame can be a double-edged sword.
Online anonymity is a double-edged sword: it protects activists but also trolls.

mistake.wrong: It's a sword with two edges.
mistake.right: It's a double-edged sword.
mistake.note: Idioms are fixed. Translating سلاح ذو حدين word for word breaks the idiom.

senses.def: to argue about very small differences that are not important
ex: Let's not split hairs over the wording.

senses.def: a matter about which people disagree, or one that is no longer important
senses.ar: مسألة خلافية؛ أمر لم يَعُد مهماً
ex: Whether he knew is a moot point now.
It's a moot point whether the plan would have worked.

mistake.wrong: It's a mute point.
mistake.right: It's a moot point.
mistake.note: moot /muːt/ and mute /mjuːt/ sound different and mean different things.

senses.def: to say that you support something without doing anything to help it
ex: The company only pays lip service to diversity.

senses.def: to do what people in authority tell you to do, even if you do not agree
ex: Ministers are expected to toe the party line.

mistake.wrong: You must tow the line.
mistake.right: You must toe the line.
mistake.note: toe (إصبع القدم), not tow (يسحب).

senses.def: short and clear, expressing what needs to be said without unnecessary words
ex: Keep your answers concise.
a concise summary of the report

senses.def: an official list of names or things
ex: The teacher took the register.
the electoral register

senses.def: the style of language, grammar and words used in particular situations
ex: Emails to friends use an informal register.
Match the register to your reader.

also.def: to put information, especially your name, on an official list
ex: You must register for the course by Friday.

senses.def: special importance or attention given to something
ex: The course places emphasis on speaking.
Inversion adds emphasis and a formal tone.

mistake.wrong: He emphasized on the importance of practice.
mistake.right: He emphasized the importance of practice. / He put emphasis on the importance of practice.
mistake.note: The verb emphasize has no preposition. The noun emphasis takes on.

senses.def: to suggest that someone or something would be good or suitable
ex: Can you recommend a good dictionary?
I'd recommend this book to anyone.

senses.def: to advise someone that something should be done
ex: It is recommended that new computers be purchased.
I recommend booking early.

mistake.wrong: Can you recommend me a hotel? / I recommend you to book early.
mistake.right: Can you recommend a hotel (to me)? / I recommend booking early. / I recommend that you book early.
mistake.note: In careful English, do not put the person straight after recommend.

senses.def: a thought or belief about something or someone
ex: In my opinion, uniforms are a good idea.
What's your opinion of the new manager?

mistake.wrong: According to my opinion, ...
mistake.right: In my opinion, ... / In my view, ...
mistake.note: Use according to for other people's opinions or sources, never for your own.

senses.def: despite the fact that
ex: Although cars are convenient, they pollute the air.
She came to work although she was ill.

mistake.wrong: Although it was raining, but we went out.
mistake.right: Although it was raining, we went out. / It was raining, but we went out.
mistake.note: Use although OR but, never both. Arabic says رغم أن... لكن, English does not.

senses.def: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something just said
ex: Cars are convenient. However, they pollute the air.

senses.def: in whatever way or to whatever degree
ex: However hard I try, I can't remember her name.

mistake.wrong: Cars are convenient, however they pollute the air.
mistake.right: Cars are convenient. However, they pollute the air. / Cars are convenient; however, they pollute the air.
mistake.note: however is not a conjunction like but. Start a new sentence or use a semicolon.

senses.def: an opinion that someone gives you about what you should do
ex: Can you give me some advice?
My teacher gave me a good piece of advice.

mistake.wrong: He gave me many advices. / I advice you to rest.
mistake.right: He gave me a lot of advice. / I advise you to rest.
mistake.note: advice (noun, /s/) is uncountable. advise (verb, /z/) is the action.

senses.def: facts about a situation, person or event
ex: For more information, visit our website.
I need some information about the course.

mistake.wrong: I have many informations.
mistake.right: I have a lot of information. / I have several pieces of information.
mistake.note: information is uncountable in English, even though معلومات is plural in Arabic.

senses.def: to talk about a subject with someone and tell each other your ideas
ex: We need to discuss the budget.
They discussed what to do next.

mistake.wrong: Let's discuss about the problem.
mistake.right: Let's discuss the problem. / Let's talk about the problem.
mistake.note: discuss has no preposition. The noun does: a discussion about the problem.

senses.def: to make something clear or easy to understand by giving details
ex: Can you explain this rule to me?
He explained why he was late.

mistake.wrong: Can you explain me this?
mistake.right: Can you explain this to me?
mistake.note: explain + thing + to + person. Never explain me.

senses.def: having a husband or wife
ex: They have been married for ten years.
She's married to a doctor.

mistake.wrong: She is married with a doctor. / He married with her.
mistake.right: She is married to a doctor. / He married her.
mistake.note: married to (adjective); marry + person, with no preposition. متزوج من is not married with.

senses.def: something that you agree to do or give to someone in order to end an argument
ex: Both sides made concessions to reach an agreement.

senses.def: the act of admitting that something is true, especially in an argument
ex: A good essay makes a concession before rejecting the other view.
